questions.question: Which brackets are used to define a dictionary in Python?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Dictionaries use curly braces { key: value }.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dictionaries are enclosed in curly braces {}.

questions.question: How do you access the value associated with key 'email' in user_dict?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Square bracket notation with the key name retrieves the value.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Access dictionary values with square brackets: dict[key].

questions.question: Can a dictionary contain duplicate keys?
options: No, keys must be unique (reassigning overwrites the old value)
Yes, as many duplicate keys as you want
Only if they have different values
questions.correct_answer: No, keys must be unique (reassigning overwrites the old value)
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Dictionary keys are unique identifiers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Duplicate keys are not permitted; duplicate assignments overwrite existing keys.

questions.question: What error occurs if you try to access a non-existent key with dict[missing_key]?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Looking up a missing key with square brackets raises a KeyError.
